what: The photo curls like paper from the bottom-right corner, tilted 30° around a cylinder (radius = Rolled by the photo’s 1/2π), it curls up to the top left and vanishes — tied to scroll (default: from when the top edge of the sheet touches the top of the screen, over 85% of the screen) as the curl position goes from -0.15 → 1.25. The cylinder’s top shows the paper back (cylinder lighting .82 to 1×), when the cylinder empties the photo face inside is visible, and the flat photo just before the curl gets a faint shade. WebGL (three) shader

options.trigger: Scroll reference — selector of the ancestor wrapping the panel (closest), default the panel itself
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: Photo to be rolled up (child) — If so, that image is used, and otherwise (.wf-img placeholder) the background, diagonal and label are drawn and used. Sits in the middle half of the panel
options.--fx-paper: Paper back color (CSS variable), default var(--kf-surface)

note: The plane is twice the size of the photo — the photo sits in the center half (25% to 75%) and the surround is where the curled paper turns over. The plane needs an explicit size. three is the cjs build in library/_vendor/three@0.185.0, so loading this folder’s three-global.js before it exposes it as window.THREE. If WebGL is unavailable the photo just stays standing

from.where: index.js makeCurl (.yf-about About photo) — original AboutSection: three r185 shader, 30° rotation axis, cylinder radius 1/(2π), progress -0.15→1.25, ScrollTrigger top top → +=85%, paper back side .82+.18×lighting
